We really tried hard to keep to the core things of God of War, of. . . start off the game for Sons of Sparta killing a cyclops, ripping his eye out. You know, we really want to make it feel right at home for the fanslike right at the very start of the game. God of War to this pointhas lived in the 3D space. So bringing that experience, that combat,that engaging, fluid movementinto a 2D space took a lot of work and planning,but Mega Cat brought that plan to us from the get go. One of the considerations that we had whentranslating a 3D action series into 2Dwas how the combat would flow smoothlybecause you're taking something from a 3D plane and thenlimiting it to just 2D, two planes. Some of the animations are taken directly from legacy God of War games,and we have developed a special tool to essentiallytake the animations from those and then convert them to 2D sprite sheets. We send it off to our pixel team to essentially draw over with pixelsto create those animations. Players will definitely seesome of the old classics like wraiths,minotaurs,gorgons. If you've ever seen any of these creatures fromthe legacy God of War gamesyou'll get to see them in thisnew, reimagined way. We wanted to bring in a lot of new enemies to the game too,but still kind of keep things to that classic Greek feel to it all. So one of my personal favorites we brought in was the lampades enemy. It's a three-bodied woman that's kind offloating on a spiral thing that shoots out fire at the player. The God of War franchise has alwaysbeen known for its larger than lifeboss battles against Greek monstersfrom myth and lore. And we've been able to create some lost legendsthat people may not be familiar withand bring them to life in ways that pixel art's never been done before. The most important things to keep from God of War for this gamehas been making sure that Kratos is fun to play. That Kratos feels cool to move around, and has great visualsaccompanying with each attack that hits hard, hits fast, and is fun. Kratos' base kit in Sons of Sparta is all about a Spartan training. It's all about the Spartan weapons, the spear and shield,and how he uses those in combat. Throughout the game, though, you begin tostart attaching things to your spearand start attaching things to your shield. Then you start to discover that there's these magical elements. Animation is very importantto having satisfying combat. I think really sellingthe blow of an axe,we see that spear go through the enemy,the feeling of the combat and really feeling like Kratos. The system that I lovethe most about the gameis definitely the sub-weapon systemand how it is tied to the gods, and how it's incorporatedinto the combat system is very much my favorite thing. Through each Olympian giftNot only are you unlocking a rangeof abilities augmented by the giftfrom the respective Olympian god, but you're also using it to your advantageto bolster your strength to defeat these monstersin a just absolutely stunning way. Between all these old enemies and these new enemiesand these themes of the game of, you know, this coming of age,we have a wide variety of things for you to fight and kill and challenge you. Don't be afraid to use all of your weapons to just mess with the world. There's a lot of interactable things. If you think something look suspicious, just give it a shot,it might be something interesting. Expect a lot of hidden boss fightsthat you might not think to look for. Sons of Sparta has it all for you. We have everything you'd expect as far as exploration and combat,but now it's attached to this unbelievable IP and this story element. If you're new to the God of War series, this is a prequel this is where it all starts,so it's the perfect entry point. Everything you love about the God of War experience is here in this game. That's a lot to do with Mega Cat taking all of those main points to heart. Is there incredible combat? Yes. Is the narrative strong throughout and makes you feel something? Yes. And finally, is the world around you one that you can get lost in? Yes. It is a God of War game through and through and one you are going to love.
